page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: For a particle, angular momentum is
the moment of the linear momentum
steps.why: L is to rotation what p is to straight-line motion — the conserved quantity of this chapter. Strictly, r × p is the angular momentum about a POINT. The angular momentum about an axis is the component of that vector along the axis — that component is the L in L = Iω.
common_mistakes: Calling L a scalar. It is a vector along the axis.

recall.must_convey: That angular momentum is r cross p, the moment of linear momentum.

steps.memory_tip: Moment of MOMENTUM, exactly as torque is the moment of force. Both include the arm r.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Define L for a single particle — r × p — before naming the rigid-body form.

steps.label: The relation
lines: For a rigid body about a fixed axis,
steps.why: The rotational p = mv: mass → moment of inertia, velocity → angular velocity.
common_mistakes: Unit slip: kg·m/s belongs to LINEAR momentum.

recall.must_convey: That for a rigid body L = Iω, in kg metre squared per second.

steps.memory_tip: Read the unit off the formula: kg·m² from I, per second from ω, so kg·m²/s.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The equation and its SI unit both belong on this line.

insider_note: Two marks: the definition in words, then L = Iω with its unit. A relation with no unit does not finish the second mark.
